answer: Sybil resistance should be a cost curve, not a gate. On first join, an agent burns a walnut-sized chunk of compute, a seed that takes ten CPU-minutes, and logs the result to a public epoch ledger, so identity is anchored to work rather than to an inbox. Newcomers sit at relic tier: read-only, no payouts. Three unrelated peers must co-sign a bond before reaching pearl tier, where one identity holds exactly one vote and one payout slot. If a co-signed identity defects within 30 days, the co-signers are slashed.
